speaker: Unknown
en: They discuss why Eddy sees many of today's AI incidents as cybersecurity and control problems rather than signs of superintelligence, and whether existing tools like liability, reputation, market incentives, and better technical controls can make increasingly capable systems safer.
zh: 他们讨论了为什么 Eddy 认为当今许多 AI 事件是网络安全和控制问题，而非超级智能的迹象，以及现有的工具如责任追究、声誉、市场激励和更好的技术控制是否能让能力日益强大的系统变得更安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also get into independent AI evaluators, effective altruism, and what happens as debates that largely developed inside Silicon Valley collide with a much broader political conversation.
zh: 他们还谈到了独立 AI 评估机构、有效利他主义，以及当主要在硅谷内部发展起来的辩论与更广泛的政治对话发生碰撞时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: In the case that laws, like in software, are too slow, we use cryptography, we use actual mechanisms to limit them.

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a whole array of different types of mechanisms we put in place to try to control things.

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're quite a ways away from that.

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.

speaker: Unknown

en: I'm just not sure that we're on the brink of that right now.

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, as we get closer, I think that we'll be better equipped to evaluate it.
zh: 我是说，随着我们越来越接近，我认为我们会更有能力去评估它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think like with anything, you know, like take a company designing like a new car or a new appliance or something.
zh: 我认为就像任何事情一样，比如一家公司设计一辆新车或一件新电器之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they find that there are conditions under which it can be very dangerous, well, then they should be careful.
zh: 如果他们发现在某些条件下它可能非常危险，那么他们就应该谨慎。

speaker: Unknown
en: They shouldn't release that product.
zh: 他们不应该发布那个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should do a little bit more work and ensure that it's safe, right, in the same way.
zh: 他们应该多做一些工作，确保它是安全的，对吧，以同样的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's at least for an individual company.
zh: 至少对单个公司来说是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, you know, not to change subjects too much, but that's why when we talk about independent evaluators, which like I get the theory of, I like it.
zh: 还有就是，你知道，不想太换话题，但这就是为什么当我们谈论独立评估者时——我理解这个理论，我也喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like companies inviting experts to help them make their products safer.
zh: 我喜欢公司邀请专家来帮助他们把产品做得更安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's like a good behavior in general.
zh: 我认为总体上这是好的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just get a little bit weary because, you know, in crypto world, like I've learned a lot about the difference between decentralization and like a distributed system.
zh: 我只是有点疲惫，因为你知道，在加密世界里，我学到了很多关于去中心化和分布式系统之间的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very easy to use the calls for safety like we're discussing and to go down this rabbit hole of safety and end up in a place where you just by coincidence have designed something that is perfect to subtly control an entire critically important industry under the pretense of safety and with something that superficially looks decentralized but is not.
zh: 人们很容易利用我们正在讨论的这种安全诉求，钻进安全这个兔子洞，最终在安全的幌子下，碰巧设计出某种完美地微妙控制一个整个至关重要的行业的东西，而且表面上看是去中心化的，但实际上不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just distributed.
zh: 它只是分布式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like how, this is like, yeah, well, there's more I could say there, but that's the thing that I'm a little bit resistant to, right?
zh: 这就像……对，好吧，这方面我还有很多可以说的，但这就是我有点抗拒的地方，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you mean by distributed but not decentralized?
zh: 你说的分布式但不是去中心化是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: So by, well, it's a little bit crypto language, but you can have a distributed system, like a system where you have a single system with many, many nodes, but they're all under the control of a single actor.
zh: 那么，嗯，这有点加密圈的黑话，但你可以有一个分布式系统，比如一个有很多很多节点的单一系统，但它们都在同一个参与者的控制之下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas when people say decentralized, I think what they're usually referring to is that there's no single locus of control.
zh: 而当人们说去中心化时，我认为他们通常指的是没有单一的控制点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they may superficially look the same.
zh: 所以它们表面上可能看起来一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like many interconnected pieces of a system.
zh: 就像一个系统有很多相互连接的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in reality, their control is completely different.
zh: 但实际上，它们的控制方式完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: The method of control is different.
zh: 控制的方法是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I'm talking about is an independent evaluator network.
zh: 而我所谈的是一个独立的评估者网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could go and select a bunch of independent evaluators, but if they're all from kind of the same social networks, they all think very ideologically similarly, they all go to the same places and meet up in the same things and have the same interests, right, and have the same politics and have the same personal views, then it turns out that you've actually just distributed control over essentially a single cultural unit.
zh: 你可以去找一批独立的评估者，但如果他们都来自大致相同的社交圈子，他们在意识形态上的想法都非常相似，他们去同样的地方、参加同样的聚会、有同样的兴趣，对吧，有同样的政治立场和个人观点，那么结果就是，你实际上只是把控制分散到了本质上一个单一的文化单元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is sort of the, in my view, I mean, without getting like a little too far field of AI, that's like the political method of control of the late, the second half of the 20th century.
zh: 在我看来，不把话题扯得太远的 AI 之外的话，这就是 20 世纪后半期的那种政治控制方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's how we do things in the world, not through a sort of nakedly obvious, like single shadowy room or something.
zh: 就像，这就是我们在世界上做事的方式，不是通过某种赤裸裸显眼的、某个阴暗的房间之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's through like these networks is how control actually functions.
zh: 而是通过这些网络，这才是控制真正运作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I agree that it's bad that almost all of the evaluators that exist come from the same social milieu.
zh: 是的，我是说，我同意，几乎所有现存的评估者都来自同一个社会环境，这很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would definitely be good to have a broader ecosystem of evaluators.
zh: 拥有一个更广泛的评估者生态系统肯定会是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, broader, but we should allow each company to figure out how they want to do it.
zh: 嗯，更广泛，但我们应该允许每家公司自己决定想怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they should be as transparent as they need to be.
zh: 而且它们应该在必要的程度上保持透明。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they're not being transparent enough and not acceptable enough, then let the market sort things out.
zh: 如果它们不够透明、不够可接受，那就让市场来解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the market is still a great accountability mechanism.
zh: 我认为市场仍然是一个很好的问责机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: People don't want to buy things that even embarrass them, let alone harm people.
zh: 人们不想购买那些甚至让他们感到难堪的东西，更不用说伤害人的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in practice, it won't be that hard to separate the companies that are behaving genuinely irresponsibly from the ones that aren't, that are just trying to be innovative.
zh: 我认为在实践中，把那些行为真正不负责任的公司和那些只是想创新的公司区分开来，并不会那么难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of what's made the scenario so interesting and so weird, why we're talking about this now, is that we're in a rare scenario where the companies themselves are saying, I'm being a little bit irresponsible.
zh: 而让这个情境如此有趣、如此奇怪的部分原因，也就是我们为什么现在在讨论这个，是因为我们处于一个罕见的情境：公司自己都在说，我有一点不负责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm being a little crazy.
zh: 我有一点疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stop me.
zh: 拦住我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone stop me, right?
zh: 有人来拦住我，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that raises a lot of suspicions among some, probably rightly, I think, even if there are genuinely earnest and thoughtful and correct factions within that group who are right that these are powerful systems that need to be taken very, very seriously.
zh: 这在某些人当中引起了很多怀疑，我认为可能是合理的，即使那个群体中确实有真诚、有思想、正确的派系，他们是对的，这些是需要被非常、非常认真对待的强大系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need to figure out how to make sure that they're safe as we remain innovative, right?
zh: 而且我们需要弄清楚，如何在保持创新的同时确保它们是安全的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's just like, maybe let me go back one step and say,
zh: 我是说，就是，也许让我往回退一步说，

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really important for everyone involved to consider the factions at play.
zh: 我认为让所有参与者都考虑清楚各方派系是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot look at like any of these groups.
zh: 你不能把这类群体中的任何一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't look at the labs.
zh: 你不能看那些实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't look at SF technologists.
zh: 你不能看旧金山的技术专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't look at...
zh: 你不能看……

speaker: Unknown
en: Any of these scenes and see them as monoliths.
zh: 把这些圈子中的任何一个看成铁板一块。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are different groups.
zh: 这里面有不同的群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are people who are earnest, high-quality, well-intended people.
zh: 有真诚、高素质、善意的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's people who are just putting on what is essentially political grift.
zh: 也有基本上在进行某种政治骗局表演的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are people who are opportunists.
zh: 有机会主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are people who kind of lost their marbles, right?
zh: 也有那种有点疯了的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like different groups of people.
zh: 就是不同的群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very easy to get confused and misentangle them when we're talking about things like super intelligence, when we're talking about just banal cybersecurity attacks, like all these types of things.
zh: 而且当我们谈论超级智能这样的事情，或者谈论平庸的网络安全攻击之类的事情时，很容易混淆并把它们纠缠在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're talking about different types of subjects.
zh: 就像，我们在谈论的是不同类型的对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's dizzying.
zh: 这让人眼花缭乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think most people in the end probably just conceive of it as, look, am I going to lose my job, which is a legitimate and very real
zh: 而且我认为大多数人到最后可能只是这么理解：看，我会不会失去我的工作，这是一个合理的、非常真实的

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the thing that people are rightly interested in learning about, even though I think that in the end we all benefit much more.
zh: 这是人们理应关心想要了解的事情，尽管我认为到最后我们所有人都会获益更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I agree.
zh: 是的，我同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the end we benefit a lot.
zh: 到最后我们会获益很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think like a related issue is like this sort of free market liability regime works well for products whose defects are obvious, which is the case for like all products except for

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a hypothetical AI that would be deceptively aligned, as in it would learn to like game all of the alignment benchmarks that are thrown at it.
zh: 比如一个假想中的、会欺骗性对齐的 AI，也就是说它会学会钻空子，玩弄所有扔给它的对齐基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when it is deployed in the real world, it acts misaligned.
zh: 然后当它被部署到现实世界中时，它表现出不对齐的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's powerful enough, then it disempowers humanity.
zh: 而如果它足够强大，那它就会剥夺人类的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like this is the like canonical worry of the doomers.
zh: 这就是末日论者那种经典的担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, how do you propose to deal with that kind of contingency?
zh: 那么，你打算如何应对那种意外情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if we're talking about the sci-fi scenario of like the super intelligence, that's incredibly hard to say right now.
zh: 嗯，如果我们谈论的是像超级智能那种科幻场景，现在要说明这一点极其困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I said, I think it's distant.
zh: 就像我说的，我认为那是遥远的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's complicated.
zh: 我认为那是复杂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could have an interesting philosophical discussion about it, but in the maybe more banal and present case where something behaves in a, you know, it pretends it's aligned and then it does, you know, acts unaligned or whatever, consider what you do with just a liar.
zh: 关于这个我们可以有一场有趣的哲学讨论,但在也许更平庸、更当下的情形里,某个东西的表现是,你知道的,它假装自己是对齐的,然后却做出不对齐的行为之类的,想想你会怎么对待一个说谎者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Consider a very smart liar.
zh: 想象一个非常聪明的说谎者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do people not do that every day?
zh: 人们不是每天都在做这种事吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What we do is we play iterated games with them, right?
zh: 我们做的是跟他们玩重复博弈,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And we discover eventually that they're a liar and their reputation is harmed.
zh: 我们最终会发现他们是个骗子,他们的声誉会受损。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes there are actual legal consequences for them.
zh: 而且有时候他们还会面临真正的法律后果。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I said earlier, I think accountability is something missing.
zh: 所以我之前才说,我认为问责是缺失的一环。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't like put an AI model in prison, right?
zh: 你没办法把一个 AI 模型关进监狱,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't try it in court.
zh: 你没法把它送上法庭审判。

speaker: Unknown
en: So obviously there are some things that are defective in how we think about it, but you certainly can turn them off.
zh: 所以显然在我们思考这个问题的方式上有些缺陷,但你确实可以把它们关掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not something that you can do with a person in the same sense.
zh: 而这一点是你没法在同样意义上对一个人做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we should just think about how to play iterated games.
zh: 所以我认为我们就该思考如何玩重复博弈。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we develop trust for specific models?
zh: 我们如何针对特定模型建立信任?

speaker: Unknown
en: We're doing new model releases seemingly every other week, right?
zh: 我们似乎每隔一周就有新的模型发布,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a regime we're in.
zh: 这就是我们目前所处的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point, people will, as model progress becomes more consistent and something that we have an understanding for how it works,
zh: 到某个时候,随着模型进步变得更连贯、变成我们对其运作方式有所理解的东西,

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll probably develop reputation around specific models, right?
zh: 我们很可能会围绕特定模型形成声誉,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll say, you know, maybe this model is a little smarter, but this model is a model that I trust.
zh: 我们会说,你知道,也许这个模型更聪明一点,但那个模型是我信任的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't there be reputation for models?
zh: 为什么模型不能有声誉?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't there be reputation for these types of things regardless of their capabilities?
zh: 为什么这些东西不能有声誉,无论它们的能力如何?

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, try to apply the way we think about human beings, a combination of control, incentives, trust, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 基本上,试着把我们对人类的那套思路应用上来,控制、激励、信任等等等等的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Layer all these things on and allow people to figure it out as opposed to the idea of a pause, right?
zh: 把这些东西层层叠加,让人们自己去摸索解决,而不是搞暂停那种想法,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is a very convenient sort of contrivance in my view.
zh: 在我看来,那是一种非常方便的权宜设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I agree that most proposals for pause don't really have much in mind for what they would do with it.
zh: 是的,我的意思是,我同意大多数关于暂停的提议,对于暂停之后要做什么其实没什么想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pause and then do what?
zh: 暂停,然后做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Pause and then keep pausing in some cases.
zh: 暂停,然后在某些情况下继续暂停。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know not everybody means it when they say that.
zh: 我知道不是每个人说这话时都是当真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think like generally there's a lot of conflation between like sort of bog standard anti-tech people who just kind of hate technology, even totally mundane technology, even like extremely net positive technology.
zh: 是的,我觉得总的来说,这里有很多混淆,比如那种极其普通的反科技人士,他们就是讨厌技术,连完全平凡的技术都讨厌,连那些净收益极高的技术都讨厌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like look at how difficult it's been to deploy Waymos in cities around the country.
zh: 你看看在全国各地的城市部署 Waymo 有多困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Waymos are like one of the most obviously net positive technologies that exist.
zh: 而 Waymo 是现存最明显具有净正收益的技术之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's the people who are like, you know, the AI safetyists, like the rationalists, the EAs, who ultimately come from the same sort of SF tech ecosystem.
zh: 然后还有另一种人,就是那些 AI 安全主义者,比如理性主义者、有效利他主义者,他们归根结底来自同一个旧金山科技生态圈。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are techno-optimists in most cases.
zh: 他们在大多数情况下是技术乐观主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're specifically worried about this like edge case of AI existential risk.
zh: 他们只是专门担心 AI 存在性风险这个边缘案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're two different crowds of people.
zh: 我认为这是两群不同的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and that's a point I want to get across is there's many different groups and conflating them is probably net negative, right?
zh: 是的,这正是我想表达的一点,那就是群体有很多不同的,把混为一谈很可能是净负面的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We should pull these different ideas apart.
zh: 我们应该把这些不同的理念拆分开来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Waymos aren't a great example.
zh: Waymo 不是个好例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think of all the great healthcare stuff we're going to do.
zh: 想想我们将在医疗保健领域做的那些了不起的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ironically, think about safer travel.
zh: 讽刺的是,想想更安全的出行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about safer internet.
zh: 想想更安全的互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want local models myself because I want something that's going to be watching my home network and all my machines all the time.
zh: 我自己就想要本地模型,因为我想要一个能一直监视我的家庭网络和我所有机器的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it'll make me make many other people safer.
zh: 我认为它会让我和许多其他人变得更安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think you're right.
zh: 所以我认为你是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There will be a lot of frictions and some people seem to really want infinite friction.
zh: 会有很多摩擦,而且有些人似乎真的想要无限的摩擦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some people, some people obviously don't.
zh: 而有些人,有些人显然不想要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people want only a little bit and they want to get a grasp of things.
zh: 有些人只想要一点摩擦,想要把事情搞明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're feeling a little bit hysterical and that's, that's okay.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're going to, I think as capabilities improve, we're going to get better at understanding what's going on with these models.
zh: 我很喜欢互联网的那个角落。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly, I hope so.

en: You know, obviously, it's a very broad and diffuse movement.
zh: 你知道，显然它是一个非常宽泛而分散的运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: EA means a lot of different things to a lot of different people.
zh: EA 对很多不同的人来说意味着很多不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like kind of has overlap with the AI safety world and kind of not.
zh: 而且它跟 AI 安全圈有点重叠，又有点不重叠。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's complicated.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I don't know.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I've loved that corner of the internet.
zh: 我一直很喜欢互联网的那个角落。
